summary: Microburst smoothing credit omission after tag-normalization change caused missing invoice credit
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that a $3,120 smoothing credit (hourly buffer credit) that usually offsets microburst reprocessing was not applied on the finalized invoice for 2026-02-28. Impact: VocalIQ sees an unexpected invoice line of $3,120; customer is on Dedicated capacity and expects smoothing credits for transient microburst replays. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated cluster vocaliq-ded-1. They executed a scheduled reprocess batch (microbatch job) between 02:10-02:26 UTC that retried ~18k requests. Expected: hourly smoothing buffer credit appears as a negative line item and offsets reprocess charges. Observed: no smoothing credit; charges appear at full rate and no provisional credit was applied. The customer is requesting an explanation and provisional credit while we investigate.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer triggered batch reprocessing (internal job id: vq-job-20260228-02). 2) Postbacks emitted to /metering/postback endpoint with tag 'vocaliq-replay' and hourly window tag '2026-02-28T02:00Z'. 3) Postback reconciler processed events; expected smoothing-credit rule to detect replayed calls within hourly buffer and apply offset credit. 4) Finalized invoice does not show smoothing credit line for that hour.
logs: Selected logs and metrics: - postback-service ingest trace: trace_id=trc-7b1c02 (02:10:12 - 02:26:41 UTC) - reconciler consumer offset lag spikes at 02:12 UTC (kafka-consumer-lag: 120s) - normalization-service WARN: tag_normalization changed case-folding rule at 2026-02-27T22:45Z - smoothing-rule evaluation count: 0 for tenant vocaliq-ded-1 for hour 02:00Z. Dashboards: billing.postback.success_rate, billing.smoothing. See chart links in investigation notes.
comments: 2026-03-02 09:18 - Support (Ava Chen): Received initial report from VocalIQ billing contact (maria@vocaliq.ai). Customer provided invoice id INV-2026-02-28-5421 and sample request IDs. Escalating to billing engineering. Assigned to Diego.

2026-03-02 11:05 - Eng (Diego Morales): I pulled reconciler logs and saw a batch of postbacks that were consumed but normalized tag values changed; normalization produced 'vocaliq_replay' (underscore) while smoothing rule looks for 'vocaliq-replay' (dash). Hypothesis: recent tag-normalization change introduced a character substitution for '-' -> '_'.

2026-03-02 13:40 - Support (Ava Chen): Notified customer we are investigating and requested the full postback payloads for 02:10-02:26 UTC. Customer provided gzipped postback archive and sample HMAC headers.

2026-03-03 08:22 - Eng (Diego Morales): Confirmed normalization PR #482 (merged 2026-02-27) introduced a unicode normalization step that collapsed non-ASCII dash characters into underscore for legacy clients. This affected rule matching. Opening fix PR to add alias matching and backfill path.
2026-03-04 16:55 - Finance (Liam Patel): Requested estimated provisional credit amount for customer while backfill runs. Support asked Eng for estimate.

2026-03-05 10:12 - Eng (Diego Morales): Backfill job queued; estimated credit to grant: $3,120. Patch to normalization-service deployed to canary (postback-service v1.14.2) and passed smoke tests. Planning to run backfill during low traffic window 2026-03-06 03:00 UTC.

2026-03-06 15:30 - Support (Ava Chen): Informed VocalIQ that provisional credit $3,120 will be applied to account as a temporary invoice adjustment; final reconciliation after backfill will confirm. Customer acknowledged and requested follow-up post-backfill.
investigation_notes: Normalization change: PR #482 added NFKC normalization and a fallback mapping that unintentionally maps unicode en-dash and em-dash to underscore rather than preserving ASCII hyphen. Regression occurred in the tag canonicalization path.
Rule mismatch: smoothing-credit rule performs exact match on normalized_tag == 'vocaliq-replay' and did not include alias set containing underscore variant.

Consumption path: kafka consumer consumed all postbacks; commit offsets indicate messages were processed; however smoothing rule counter did not increment because normalized tag did not match rule predicate.
Reconciler metrics: smoothing.applied_rate for tenant vocaliq-ded-1 dropped to 0 between 02:10-02:26; other tenants unaffected. Suggests tenant-specific tags used by customer triggered the bug.
Potential risk: Similar tag-normalization changes could affect other tenants that use non-ASCII punctuation or custom tagging. Recommend audit of normalization mapping and rule predicates.
Related artifacts: slack thread #support-billing (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C07BILL/ppg123), Grafana panel billing.smoothing.
resolution: Mitigation applied: provisional credit of $3,120 applied to VocalIQ account (credit memo CM-2026-03-06-97). Finance notified customer; adjustment appears on account immediately.

Fix deployed: normalization-service patch (postback-service v1.14.3) restores ASCII hyphen preservation and adds alias matching for common variants. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/postback-service/pull/485 (merged 2026-03-05).

Backfill: backfill job executed 2026-03-06 03:00 UTC and applied smoothing credits retroactively; reconciliation job validated 18,432 postbacks matched and credit of $3,120 reconciled. Final invoice adjustment will reflect removal of provisional credit and replace with backfilled credit (net zero change).

Post-deploy monitoring: Added alert smoothing.applied_rate_drop and runbook step to check normalization mappings after any change. Added unit/regression tests for tag canonicalization and rule aliasing.

Follow-up tasks: - ENG-OPS: add alias set to smoothing rules to handle hyphen/underscore variants (ticket INT-334). - Billing: confirm final invoice lines and close credit memo. - CS: send summary to VocalIQ with timeline and remediation details.
